issues.description: PR conflates three unrelated changes (tests, README rewrite, FAQ addition) under a test-only title
issues.detail: Stated goal is adding POST tests, but the diff also rewrites the README example with handler signature reorder, status formatting swap, and stream-to-bounded_stream change, plus a new FAQ section. Reviewers cannot separate the value-changing edits from cosmetic reflow. Split into independent commits, each with a rationale.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is an undocumented semantic change that the new test depends on
issues.detail: things_advanced.py silently changes body = req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(). These have different preconditions around Content-Length. The change is load-bearing for the new 400 assertion but is unmentioned in the PR description and has no stated rationale. The production code was bent to make the test green rather than to satisfy a documented contract.

issues.description: New 400 test pins an incidental behavior rather than a documented contract
issues.detail: resp4 expects 400 for empty body with Content-Length: 1, but that outcome only exists because of the quietly-changed bounded_stream call in this same PR. The contract for 'Content-Length disagrees with body' is never named. The test asserts the current accident rather than an invariant. Name the contract first, then write the test.

issues.description: FAQ example fabricates handler behavior to teach a 400, with nested control flow and unclear lesson
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post re-reads Content-Length and returns 400 for empty body via nested if/else. The actual lesson (header override in simulate_post) is one line; the rest is scaffolding that teaches a wrong mental model and uses nested selection where three flat branches would be readable. Shrink the example to its actual point.

issues.description: FAQ example uses parenthesized assert, a known Python footgun
issues.detail: assert(result.status == ...) reads like a function call and trains readers toward the broken assert(x, y) form, which is a tuple and always truthy. In published documentation code that teaches testing, write assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400 without parentheses.

issues.description: Omnibus test function bundles multiple independent POST cases with shared state and duplicated headers
issues.detail: test_things_advanced appends both happy-path POST and malformed-length POST in one function with shared mutable app state and hardcoded Authorization/Content-Type headers repeated inline. A failure in resp3 masks resp4. Split into named tests per assertion and extract common headers to a fixture or local dict.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches strong consensus that this PR is three patches in a trench coat: a reasonable test addition is bundled with an undocumented semantic change (req.stream to req.bounded_stream) and a sprawling FAQ example that fabricates the behavior it claims to teach. The new 400 test pins an incidental outcome of the silently-changed implementation rather than a stated contract about Content-Length disagreement. The README rewrite further smuggles a handler-signature reorder and status-formatting swap under cosmetic reflow. Action: split the PR, name the Content-Length contract, shrink the FAQ example to its real lesson, and fix the parenthesized assert.
